figures.applies: UK audiovisual performers (CREATe/BECS survey, 2024); Australian professional actors and directors (Artists as Workers, 2024).
figures.replaces: The game's share of working actors who trained: about four in five, typically three years.

figures.finding: In IMDb's worldwide record of actors since 1888, about 69% of actors and 68% of actresses have careers spanning a single year; longer careers and high activity become exponentially rarer.
figures.applies: Worldwide film and TV credits on IMDb, 1888 to the late 2010s (Williams, Lacasa and Latora, Nature Communications 10:2256, 2019).
figures.replaces: The game's career-length distribution: most credited actors never work a second year; survival falls off exponentially.

sources.said: we find that the percentage of such cases is extremely high (around 69% for males and 68% for females)
one-hit wonders, i.e., actors whose career spans only a single year, are the norm rather than the exception. Long career lengths and high activity are found to be exponentially rare
